Immediate (Hours–Months):
USGS real-time streamflow
India-WRIS daily reservoir levels
Aqueduct near-real-time stress
Medium-Term (1–10 Years):
GRACE monthly groundwater anomalies
Global Surface Water Explorer annual composites
GRDC seasonal discharge trends
Long-Term (Decades–Centuries):
GRDC multi-century station records
Glacial melt projections (IPCC)
Paleo-hydrological reconstructions
Temporal Gaps & Blindspots: Aquifer depletion often invisible for 20–50 years before surface effects. Virtual water trade temporal lag poorly understood.

Immediate (Hours–Months):
OpenAQ hourly readings
AirNow real-time AQI
Copernicus CAMS daily forecasts
Medium-Term (1–10 Years):
NOAA annual CO2/CH4 trends
Global Carbon Project annual budgets
MODIS AOD seasonal analysis
Long-Term (Decades–Centuries):
Keeling Curve (1958–present)
Ice core records (800,000 years)
Global Carbon Project (1750–present)
Temporal Gaps & Blindspots: Short-lived pollutants (PM2.5) well-tracked in real-time. Long-lived GHGs have deep history. Gap: medium-term (5-10yr) local air quality trends outside wealthy nations.

Immediate (Hours–Months):
Seasonal soil tests (farmer-level)
Soil moisture sensors (where deployed)
Medium-Term (1–10 Years):
EU LUCAS 3-year survey cycle
SOC trend analysis (5-10yr windows)
Erosion rate monitoring
Long-Term (Decades–Centuries):
SoilGrids baseline (multi-decadal composite)
Desertification frontiers (decade scale)
Paleo-soil records
Temporal Gaps & Blindspots: CRITICAL GAP: Soil changes are slowest of all ecologies. Most damage invisible for 30-100 years. Real-time soil monitoring almost nonexistent globally.
